cookie-shortbread-with-icing-or-filling.title: Cookie, shortbread with icing or filling

content.title: About
content.content: Shortbread is a crumbly butter cookie made from butter, sugar and flour, often topped with icing or filled with a sweet centre. It has a delicate buttery flavour, a slightly sandy texture and a sweet note typical of traditional British biscuits.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shortbread originated in Scotland in the 19th century and quickly spread throughout the United Kingdom.
Traditionally it is cut into rectangular bars, but modern versions come in circles, hearts and decorative shapes.
Icing can be chocolate, fruit or caramel, while fillings include jam, cream, nougat or nut paste.
In the United States the equivalent is often called a “shortbread cookie” and is commonly served with tea.
The classic recipe uses only butter, without leavening agents.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates and fats provide a quick source of energy, making it a handy snack.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Butter, the main ingredient, is rich in vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Calcium and magnesium
items.content: Flour and butter contribute modest amounts of calcium and magnesium, supporting bone health and nerve function.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: Although modest, shortbread supplies plant protein from the flour.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Icing and fillings can significantly raise the sugar level, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Since wheat flour is used, the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Butter and milk‑based icing may trigger reactions in individuals with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Shortbread is calorie‑dense; moderate consumption is advised in weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The cookie can be enjoyed on its own, served with tea or coffee, used as a base for desserts and parfaits, or crumbled over ice cream and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to prevent the icing from softening.

content.title: About
content.content: Blueberry pie is a dessert made with a tender crust and a filling of fresh or frozen blueberries sweetened with sugar, often flavored with lemon juice or vanilla. The crust is baked until golden, while the berries become juicy, creating a fragrant sweet‑tart taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blueberries are considered a “superfood” because of their high antioxidant content.
The first blueberry pie recipes appeared in North America in the 19th century.
Pie crust is usually made from flour, butter, eggs, and a small amount of sugar, giving it a flaky texture.
Blueberry pie is often served with whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
There are many variations of the filling, from classic sugared berries to versions with ginger or nuts.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Blueberries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Vision support
items.content: Studies suggest regular blueberry consumption may improve visual function, especially in low‑light conditions.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Vitamin C boosts the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Both the berries and whole‑grain crust provide fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic index of berries
items.content: Blueberries cause a modest rise in blood sugar, making them suitable for moderate consumption even for diabetics.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Traditional blueberry pie can contain a significant amount of added sugar, increasing its calorie count.

items.title: Berry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to blueberries or other berries in the same family.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of berries can cause gas in people with sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Calorie‑dense crust
items.content: Butter‑rich crust is high in fat, so portion control is advisable for those watching their diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the pie warm, sliced into portions. It can be enjoyed on its own or topped with whipped cream, vanilla ice cream, yogurt, or a light dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the blueberry pie covered with plastic wrap or in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze individual slices in a freezer‑safe bag – they retain flavor for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or microwave before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Salad dressing NFS is a ready‑to‑use dressing made from vegetable oils, vinegar and aromatic herbs, specially formulated for sandwiches. It has a light creamy texture, a mildly tangy taste and subtle spice notes that enhance the flavor of meat, cheese and vegetables in a sandwich.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dressing was developed in 2021 as part of the NFS line focused on quick and tasty fast‑food solutions.
It contains extra‑virgin olive oil, making it a healthier alternative to traditional mayonnaise‑based dressings.
Salad dressing NFS contains no artificial colours or flavours.
It works well in both cold and hot sandwiches – the flavor remains stable when heated up to 80 °C.
The 250 ml bottle provides roughly 15‑20 servings depending on the amount used per sandwich.

items.title: Rich in monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olive oil helps maintain healthy cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E is an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Includes acetic acid
items.content: Vinegar can aid digestion and slow carbohydrate absorption.

items.title: Herbal extracts
items.content: Thyme, oregano and basil provide anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: The dressing is suitable for low‑sugar diets.

items.title: Allergy to vegetable oils
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to olive or sunflower oil.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The dressing contains a moderate amount of salt; people monitoring sodium intake should use it sparingly.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The vinegar may irritate the stomach lining if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Spread the dressing on bread or a bun before adding fillings, or drizzle over a finished sandwich. Ideal for hot grilled sandwiches, cold subs, and also as a dip for vegetable sticks.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dressing refrigerated at 2 °C–6 °C. Once opened, consume within 30 days. Ensure the cap is tightly closed and avoid contamination.
